messages:
Jordan (Support): Heads-up, BrightBridge just escalated — ingestion failing intermittently for new customer data feeds, looks like schema mismatch + some 502s. Ticket #BB-4921 :warning:
NotifyBot: Ticket BB-4921 severity -> P1 (automated escalation)
Elena (CSM): Ugh, renewal in 45 days for BrightBridge. This could move to risk if we don't show a fast remediation path.
Sam (CS Ops): Can you paste the error patterns and affected endpoints? I can draft comms and a short runbook for the SEs.
Jordan (Support): Errors show two classes: 
- `422` on parsing for field `customer_profile.metadata` (unexpected null)
- intermittent `502` from embed-ingest service during backfill
Here are recent logs:
```
ERROR [embed-ingest] 2026-03-18T10:03:21Z id=bb-4921 req=7f2a parse failed: null value for required key metadata
WARN  [api-proxy] 2026-03-18T10:03:22Z upstream 502 during POST /v1/ingest
```
Michael (SE): I can debug the parsing quickly — likely the feed schema changed in their SFTP dump. If we can get a sample file we can patch our parser to tolerate nulls and add a defensive migration. ETA ~3-4 hours to a hotfix if they can share sample.
Elena (CSM): I'll ask BrightBridge for a sample now. Also we should propose an immediate workaround for their pipeline so they don't hit the 502s during business hours.
Sam (CS Ops): Draft comms plan below — aim to acknowledge in 30m, provide workaround within 3h, hotfix + regression test in 24h, and a postmortem + feedback capture before renewal check-in.
Sam (CS Ops): COMM TEMPLATE (short):
```
Hi <Name>,
We saw intermittent ingestion failures and 502s affecting your backfill. We're actively investigating and have a short-term workaround to keep data flowing: please pause full backfill and restart incremental batches every 30m until we confirm the fix. Our SEs can apply a temporary parser tolerance if you share a sample file. We'll update you within 3 hours with next steps.
— BrightBridge support team
```
Elena (CSM): Nice. For exec-facing updates I will add a one-line impact + committed timings. Also schedule a quick enablement session after the fix so their ops know how to avoid schema drift.
Michael (SE): If they can SFTP a sample to `sftp://redwood-temp/brightbridge/` I can run a local test and push a tolerant parser to a canary pod. After canary looks good we'll rollout to production with autoscale off for 10m to monitor.
Jordan (Support): BrightBridge replied — attaching sample link: `s3://bb-corp-dumps/2026-03-18/sample-1.json` (shared). They confirmed they started a backfill at 09:50.
Sam (CS Ops): Plan tasks + owners:
- Acknowledge + workaround -> Elena (within 30m)
- Run sample + canary patch -> Michael (3-4h)
- Hotfix rollout & monitor -> Support + SE (24h)
- Postmortem + renewal note -> Sam/Elena (48h)
- Capture feedback via short survey after enablement -> Elena (post-fix)
Elena (CSM): I'm pinging their CTO for approval to pause full backfill and to confirm SFTP access. I'll include the exec note and timeline.
NotifyBot: Reminder: create-runbook task assigned to Sam (due in 4 hours)
Jordan (Support): I'll keep the ticket updated w/ logs and any 502 spikes. If we see more 502s during rollout we escalate to eng-runtime.
Michael (SE): I'll start local tests now. If parser change is trivial I will open PR and assign to @engineers-runtime for a quick review.
Elena (CSM): Good. Also let's capture two pieces of feedback for Product: (1) better schema drift alerting in console, (2) clearer guidance on backfill safety. I'll log them after the incident.
Sam (CS Ops): I'll drop a short checklist in the runbook for CS handoff post-fix (how to verify ingestion health, how to run small incremental backfills, contact points).
Jordan (Support): Thanks team — marking as handoff to CS once canary passes. Will re-assign ticket to Elena after Michael updates. :thumbsup:
